questions.text: Consider the sets $A=\{(x, y)\in\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}: x^2+y^2=25\}$, $B=\{(x, y)\in\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}: x^2+9y^2=144\}$, $C=\left\{(x, y)\in\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}: x^2+y^2\le 4\right\}$ and $D=A\cap B$. The total number of one-one functions from the set $D$ to the set $C$ is:
questions.sol:
$D$: subtracting the equations gives $8y^2=119$, so $y^2=\dfrac{119}{8}$ and $x^2=\dfrac{81}{8}$: four points (all sign choices), so $n(D)=4$.
$C$: lattice points with $x^2+y^2\le4$: $x=0$ gives 5 points, $x=\pm1$ give 3 each, $x=\pm2$ give 1 each, so $n(C)=13$.
One-one functions from a 4-element set to a 13-element set: $13\cdot12\cdot11\cdot10=17160$.

questions.text: Let $f, g: (1, \infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined as $f(x)=\dfrac{2x+3}{5x+2}$ and $g(x)=\dfrac{2-3x}{1-x}$. If the range of the function $fog: [2, 4]\to\mathbb{R}$ is $[\alpha, \beta]$, then $\dfrac{1}{\beta-\alpha}$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$2g(x)+3=\dfrac{7-9x}{1-x}$ and $5g(x)+2=\dfrac{12-17x}{1-x}$, so $f(g(x))=\dfrac{7-9x}{12-17x}$.
Its derivative has numerator $(-9)(12-17x)+17(7-9x)=11>0$, so it is increasing on $[2, 4]$.
$\alpha=f(g(2))=\dfrac{-11}{-22}=\dfrac12$, $\beta=f(g(4))=\dfrac{-29}{-56}=\dfrac{29}{56}$.
$\beta-\alpha=\dfrac{1}{56}$, so $\dfrac1{\beta-\alpha}=56$.

questions.text: Consider the equation $x^2+4x-n=0$, where $n\in[20, 100]$ is a natural number. Then the number of all distinct values of $n$, for which the given equation has integral roots, is equal to
questions.sol:
The roots are $-2\pm\sqrt{4+n}$; they are integers exactly when $4+n=k^2$ for an integer $k$.
$24\le k^2\le104$ gives $k=5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10$, i.e. $n=21, 32, 45, 60, 77, 96$.
Number of values $=6$.

questions.text: Let $A=\{1, 6, 11, 16, \ldots\}$ and $B=\{9, 16, 23, 30, \ldots\}$ be the sets consisting of the first 2025 terms of two arithmetic progressions. Then $n(A\cup B)$ is
questions.sol:
Last terms: $A$: $1+5\cdot2024=10121$; $B$: $9+7\cdot2024=14177$.
Common terms satisfy $x\equiv1\pmod5$ and $x\equiv2\pmod7$: $x=16, 51, 86, \ldots$ (an A.P. with difference 35), and they must not exceed 10121.
$16+35t\le10121$ gives $t\le288$, so there are 289 common terms.
$n(A\cup B)=2025+2025-289=3761$.

questions.text: $1+3+5^2+7+9^2+\ldots$ upto 40 terms is equal to
questions.sol:
The odd-numbered terms are $(4k-3)^2$ and the even-numbered terms are $4k-1$, $k=1, \ldots, 20$.
$\sum(4k-3)^2=16\sum k^2-24\sum k+9\cdot20=16(2870)-24(210)+180=41060$.
$\sum(4k-1)=4(210)-20=820$.
Total $=41060+820=41880$.

questions.text: For an integer $n\ge2$, if the arithmetic mean of all coefficients in the binomial expansion of $(x+y)^{2n-3}$ is 16, then the distance of the point $P(2n-1, n^2-4n)$ from the line $x+y=8$ is
questions.sol:
There are $2n-2$ coefficients with sum $2^{2n-3}$, so $\dfrac{2^{2n-3}}{2n-2}=16$; $n=5$ works ($2^7/8=16$), and the left side increases with $n$ for $n\ge3$.
$P=(9, 5)$; distance from $x+y-8=0$: $\dfrac{|9+5-8|}{\sqrt2}=\dfrac{6}{\sqrt2}=3\sqrt2$.

questions.text: Let the three sides of a triangle are on the lines $4x-7y+10=0$, $x+y=5$ and $7x+4y=15$. Then the distance of its orthocentre from the orthocentre of the tringle formed by the lines $x=0$, $y=0$ and $x+y=1$ is
questions.sol:
$4x-7y+10=0$ and $7x+4y=15$ are perpendicular (slopes $\dfrac47$ and $-\dfrac74$), so the first triangle is right-angled where they meet; solving gives $(1, 2)$, which is its orthocentre.
The second triangle is right-angled at the origin, so its orthocentre is $(0, 0)$.
Distance $=\sqrt{1+4}=\sqrt5$.

questions.text: The length of the latus-rectum of the ellipse, whose foci are $(2, 5)$ and $(2, -3)$ and eccentricity is $\dfrac45$, is
questions.sol:
Distance between the foci $2ae=8$, so $ae=4$ and $a=5$.
$b^2=a^2(1-e^2)=25-16=9$.
Latus rectum $=\dfrac{2b^2}{a}=\dfrac{18}{5}$.

questions.text: If $10\sin^4\theta+15\cos^4\theta=6$, then the value of $\dfrac{27\operatorname{cosec}^6\theta+8\sec^6\theta}{16\sec^8\theta}$ is
questions.sol:
Put $t=\sin^2\theta$: $10t^2+15(1-t)^2=6$, i.e. $25t^2-30t+9=0$, $(5t-3)^2=0$, so $\sin^2\theta=\dfrac35$, $\cos^2\theta=\dfrac25$.
$27\operatorname{cosec}^6\theta=27\cdot\dfrac{125}{27}=125$, $8\sec^6\theta=8\cdot\dfrac{125}{8}=125$, $16\sec^8\theta=16\cdot\dfrac{625}{16}=625$.
Value $=\dfrac{250}{625}=\dfrac25$.

questions.text: Considering the principal values of the inverse trigonometric functions, $\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}x+\dfrac12\sqrt{1-x^2}\right)$, $-\dfrac12<x<\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$, is equal to
questions.sol:
Put $x=\sin\theta$ with $\theta=\sin^{-1}x\in\left(-\dfrac\pi6, \dfrac\pi4\right)$, so $\sqrt{1-x^2}=\cos\theta$.
The argument is $\sin\theta\cos\dfrac\pi6+\cos\theta\sin\dfrac\pi6=\sin\left(\theta+\dfrac\pi6\right)$ with $\theta+\dfrac\pi6\in\left(0, \dfrac{5\pi}{12}\right)$, inside the principal range.
Value $=\dfrac\pi6+\sin^{-1}x$.

questions.text: Let the shortest distance between the lines $\dfrac{x-3}{3}=\dfrac{y-\alpha}{-1}=\dfrac{z-3}{1}$ and $\dfrac{x+3}{-3}=\dfrac{y+7}{2}=\dfrac{z-\beta}{4}$ be $3\sqrt{30}$. Then the positive value of $5\alpha+\beta$ is
questions.sol:
$\vec b_1\times\vec b_2=(3, -1, 1)\times(-3, 2, 4)=(-6, -15, 3)$, of length $\sqrt{270}=3\sqrt{30}$.
Joining vector $(-3, -7, \beta)-(3, \alpha, 3)=(-6, -7-\alpha, \beta-3)$; its dot product with $(-6, -15, 3)$ is $132+15\alpha+3\beta$.
$\dfrac{|132+15\alpha+3\beta|}{3\sqrt{30}}=3\sqrt{30}$ gives $15\alpha+3\beta=138$ or $-402$, i.e. $5\alpha+\beta=46$ or $-134$.
Positive value: 46.

questions.text: Let $A$ and $B$ be two distinct points on the line $L: \dfrac{x-6}{3}=\dfrac{y-7}{2}=\dfrac{z-7}{-2}$. Both $A$ and $B$ are at a distance $2\sqrt{17}$ from the foot of perpendicular drawn from the point $(1, 2, 3)$ on the line $L$. If $O$ is the origin, then $\overrightarrow{OA}\cdot\overrightarrow{OB}$ is equal to
questions.sol:
A general point of $L$ is $(6+3t, 7+2t, 7-2t)$. For the foot, $(5+3t, 5+2t, 4-2t)\cdot(3, 2, -2)=0$ gives $17+17t=0$, $t=-1$: foot $(3, 5, 9)$.
The direction $(3, 2, -2)$ has length $\sqrt{17}$, so $A$, $B$ correspond to $t=-1\pm2$: $(9, 9, 5)$ and $(-3, 1, 13)$.
$\overrightarrow{OA}\cdot\overrightarrow{OB}=-27+9+65=47$.

questions.text: Consider two vectors $\vec u=3\hat i-\hat j$ and $\vec v=2\hat i+\hat j-\lambda\hat k$, $\lambda>0$. The angle between them is given by $\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt5}{2\sqrt7}\right)$. Let $\vec v=\vec v_1+\vec v_2$, where $\vec v_1$ is parallel to $\vec u$ and $\vec v_2$ is perpendicular to $\vec u$. Then the value $\left|\vec v_1\right|^2+\left|\vec v_2\right|^2$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$\cos\theta=\dfrac{\vec u\cdot\vec v}{|\vec u||\vec v|}=\dfrac{5}{\sqrt{10}\sqrt{5+\lambda^2}}=\dfrac{\sqrt5}{2\sqrt7}$; squaring, $\dfrac{25}{10(5+\lambda^2)}=\dfrac{5}{28}$, so $\lambda^2=9$.
Since $\vec v_1\perp\vec v_2$, $|\vec v_1|^2+|\vec v_2|^2=|\vec v|^2=4+1+9=14$.

questions.text: If $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to1^+}\frac{(x-1)\left(6+\lambda\cos(x-1)\right)+\mu\sin(1-x)}{(x-1)^3}=-1$, where $\lambda, \mu\in\mathbb{R}$, then $\lambda+\mu$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Put $t=x-1\to0^+$. The numerator is $t(6+\lambda\cos t)-\mu\sin t=(6+\lambda-\mu)t+\left(\dfrac{\mu}{6}-\dfrac{\lambda}{2}\right)t^3+\cdots$.
For a finite limit, $6+\lambda-\mu=0$; then $\dfrac{\mu}{6}-\dfrac{\lambda}{2}=-1$.
With $\mu=6+\lambda$: $1+\dfrac{\lambda}{6}-\dfrac{\lambda}{2}=-1$, so $\lambda=6$, $\mu=12$ and $\lambda+\mu=18$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a continuous function satisfying $f(0)=1$ and $f(2x)-f(x)=x$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$. If $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\left\{f(x)-f\left(\frac{x}{2^n}\right)\right\}=G(x)$, then $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{10}G(r^2)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Replacing $x$ by $\dfrac{x}{2^k}$: $f\left(\dfrac{x}{2^{k-1}}\right)-f\left(\dfrac{x}{2^k}\right)=\dfrac{x}{2^k}$.
Adding for $k=1, \ldots, n$: $f(x)-f\left(\dfrac{x}{2^n}\right)=x\left(1-\dfrac{1}{2^n}\right)\to x$, so $G(x)=x$.
$\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{10}r^2=385$.

questions.text: The value of $\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1}\frac{\left(1+\sqrt{|x|-x}\right)e^x+\left(\sqrt{|x|-x}\right)e^{-x}}{e^x+e^{-x}}\,dx$ is equal to
questions.sol:
The integrand equals $\sqrt{|x|-x}+\dfrac{e^x}{e^x+e^{-x}}$.
$\dfrac{e^x}{e^x+e^{-x}}$ and its value at $-x$ add to 1, so its integral over $[-1, 1]$ is 1.
$\sqrt{|x|-x}$ is 0 for $x\ge0$ and $\sqrt{-2x}$ for $x<0$: $\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{0}\sqrt{-2x}\,dx=\sqrt2\cdot\frac23=\frac{2\sqrt2}{3}$.
Value $=1+\dfrac{2\sqrt2}{3}$.

questions.text: Let $f:[0, \infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be a differentiable function such that $f(x)=1-2x+\displaystyle\int_0^x e^{x-t}f(t)\,dt$ for all $x\in[0, \infty)$. Then the area of the region bounded by $y=f(x)$ and the coordinate axes is
questions.sol:
$f(x)=1-2x+e^x\displaystyle\int_0^x e^{-t}f(t)\,dt$, so $f(0)=1$ and $f'(x)=-2+\left(f(x)-1+2x\right)+f(x)=2f(x)+2x-3$.
A particular solution is $1-x$, so $f(x)=1-x+Ce^{2x}$; $f(0)=1$ gives $C=0$.
$y=1-x$ meets the axes at $(1, 0)$ and $(0, 1)$: area $=\dfrac12$.

questions.text: Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}\cos\theta & 0 & -\sin\theta\\ 0 & 1 & 0\\ \sin\theta & 0 & \cos\theta\end{bmatrix}$. If for some $\theta\in(0, \pi)$, $A^2=A^T$, then the sum of the diagonal elements of the matrix $(A+I)^3+(A-I)^3-6A$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
$A$ is orthogonal ($AA^T=I$), so $A^2=A^T$ gives $A^3=AA^T=I$.
Since $A$ and $I$ commute, $(A+I)^3+(A-I)^3=2A^3+6A$.
So the matrix is $2A^3=2I$, whose trace is 6.

questions.text: Let $C$ be the circle $x^2+(y-1)^2=2$, $E_1$ and $E_2$ be two ellipses whose centres lie at the origin and major axes lie on x-axis and y-axis respectively. Let the straight line $x+y=3$ touch the curves $C$, $E_1$ and $E_2$ at $P(x_1, y_1)$, $Q(x_2, y_2)$ and $R(x_3, y_3)$ respectively. Given that $P$ is the mid point of the line segment $QR$ and $PQ=\dfrac{2\sqrt2}{3}$, the value of $9(x_1y_1+x_2y_2+x_3y_3)$ is equal to __________
questions.sol:
$P$ is the foot of the perpendicular from $(0, 1)$ to $x+y=3$: $P=(1, 2)$.
Points of the line at distance $\dfrac{2\sqrt2}{3}$ from $P$: $\left(\dfrac53, \dfrac43\right)$ and $\left(\dfrac13, \dfrac83\right)$.
For $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ the line $x+y=3$ touches at $\left(\dfrac{a^2}{3}, \dfrac{b^2}{3}\right)$, so $x>y$ when $a>b$: $Q=\left(\dfrac53, \dfrac43\right)$ on $E_1$ and $R=\left(\dfrac13, \dfrac83\right)$ on $E_2$.
$9\left(2+\dfrac{20}{9}+\dfrac{8}{9}\right)=18+20+8=46$.

questions.text: Let $m$ and $n$ be the number of points at which the function $f(x)=\max\{x, x^3, x^5, \ldots, x^{21}\}$, $x\in\mathbb{R}$, is not differentiable and not continuous, respectively. Then $m+n$ is equal to __________
questions.sol:
$f$ is the maximum of continuous functions, so it is continuous everywhere: $n=0$.
$f(x)=x$ for $x\le-1$, $x^{21}$ for $-1\le x\le0$, $x$ for $0\le x\le1$ and $x^{21}$ for $x\ge1$.
At $x=-1$ the one-sided derivatives are 1 and 21; at $x=0$ they are 0 and 1; at $x=1$ they are 1 and 21. So $m=3$.
$m+n=3$.

questions.text:
Which of the following are correct expression for torque acting on a body?
A. $\vec\tau=\vec r\times\vec L$
B. $\vec\tau=\dfrac{d}{dt}\left(\vec r\times\vec p\right)$
C. $\vec\tau=\vec r\times\dfrac{d\vec p}{dt}$
D. $\vec\tau=I\vec\alpha$
E. $\vec\tau=\vec r\times\vec F$
($\vec r=$ position vector; $\vec p=$ linear momentum; $\vec L=$ angular momentum; $\vec\alpha=$ angular acceleration; $I=$ moment of inertia; $\vec F=$ force; $t=$ time)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B, D and E Only
B, C, D and E Only
questions.note: NTA's final key accepts both option (1) "B, D and E Only" and option (3) "B, C, D and E Only". Expression C is also correct, because $\dfrac{d}{dt}(\vec r\times\vec p)=\vec v\times\vec p+\vec r\times\dfrac{d\vec p}{dt}$ and $\vec v\times\vec p=0$.
questions.sol:
A: $\vec r\times\vec L$ is not a torque (wrong dimensions). B: $\vec\tau=\dfrac{d\vec L}{dt}$ with $\vec L=\vec r\times\vec p$: correct.
C: $\dfrac{d}{dt}(\vec r\times\vec p)=\vec v\times m\vec v+\vec r\times\dfrac{d\vec p}{dt}=\vec r\times\dfrac{d\vec p}{dt}$: correct.
D: $\vec\tau=I\vec\alpha$ for rotation about a fixed axis: correct. E: $\vec\tau=\vec r\times\vec F$: correct.
So B, C, D and E; the key also accepts "B, D and E Only".

questions.text: A body of mass $m$ is suspended by two strings making angles $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$ with the horizontal ceiling with tensions $T_1$ and $T_2$ simultaneously. $T_1$ and $T_2$ are related by $T_1=\sqrt3T_2$, the angles $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$ are
questions.sol:
Horizontal balance: $T_1\cos\theta_1=T_2\cos\theta_2$, so $\sqrt3\cos\theta_1=\cos\theta_2$; this needs $\cos\theta_1\le\dfrac1{\sqrt3}$, and $\theta_1=60^\circ$, $\theta_2=30^\circ$ fits.
Vertical balance: $T_1\sin60^\circ+T_2\sin30^\circ=\sqrt3T_2\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}+\dfrac{T_2}{2}=2T_2=mg$.
$T_2=\dfrac{mg}{2}$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R
Assertion A: The kinetic energy needed to project a body of mass m from earth surface to infinity is $\dfrac12$mgR, where R is the radius of earth.
Reason R: The maximum potential energy of a body is zero when it is projected to infinity from earth surface.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.sol:
To reach infinity the body needs $\dfrac{GMm}{R}=mgR$ of kinetic energy (its potential energy rises from $-mgR$ to 0), not $\dfrac12mgR$: A is false.
Gravitational potential energy $-\dfrac{GMm}{r}$ increases with $r$ and reaches its maximum value, zero, at infinity: R is true.

questions.text: If $\vec L$ and $\vec P$ represent the angular momentum and linear momentum respectively of a particle of mass 'm' having position vector as $\vec r=a\left(\hat i\cos\omega t+\hat j\sin\omega t\right)$. The direction of force is
options: Opposite to the direction of $\vec r$
Opposite to the direction of $\vec P$
Opposite to the direction of $\vec L$
Opposite to the direction of $\vec L\times\vec P$
questions.sol:
The particle moves uniformly on a circle of radius $a$: $\vec a=\dfrac{d^2\vec r}{dt^2}=-\omega^2\vec r$.
So $\vec F=m\vec a=-m\omega^2\vec r$, directed opposite to $\vec r$ (towards the centre).

questions.text: Two liquids A and B have $\theta_A$ and $\theta_B$ as contact angles in a capillary tube. If $K=\cos\theta_A/\cos\theta_B$, then identify the correct statement:
options: K is negative, then liquid A and liquid B have concave meniscus.
K is negative, then liquid A and liquid B have convex meniscus.
K is negative, then liquid A has concave meniscus and liquid B has convex meniscus.
K is zero, then liquid A has convex meniscus and liquid B has concave meniscus.
questions.sol:
A contact angle below $90^\circ$ (positive cosine) gives a concave meniscus; above $90^\circ$ (negative cosine) gives a convex one.
$K<0$ means the cosines have opposite signs, so one liquid is concave and the other convex; option (3) is such a case.
$K=0$ would mean $\theta_A=90^\circ$, a flat meniscus for A, so option (4) is wrong.

questions.text: Consider the sound wave travelling in ideal gases of $He$, $CH_4$, and $CO_2$. All the gases have the same ratio $\dfrac{P}{\rho}$, where $P$ is the pressure and $\rho$ is the density. The ratio of the speed of sound through the gases $v_{He}:v_{CH_4}:v_{CO_2}$ is given by
questions.note: NTA's final key gives option (4), which takes $\gamma=\dfrac43$ for $\mathrm{CO_2}$ (treated as a polyatomic gas). For a rigid linear $\mathrm{CO_2}$ molecule (3 translational and 2 rotational degrees of freedom) $\gamma=\dfrac75$, which would give option (2). The key is followed here.
questions.sol:
Speed of sound in a gas: $v=\sqrt{\dfrac{\gamma P}{\rho}}$; with the same $\dfrac P\rho$, $v\propto\sqrt\gamma$.
He (monatomic): $\gamma=\dfrac53$. $\mathrm{CH_4}$ (polyatomic): $\gamma=\dfrac43$. Taking $\mathrm{CO_2}$ as polyatomic as well (as NTA's key does): $\gamma=\dfrac43$.
Ratio $\sqrt{\dfrac53}:\sqrt{\dfrac43}:\sqrt{\dfrac43}$.

questions.text: Two simple pendulums having lengths $l_1$ and $l_2$ with negligible string mass undergo angular displacements $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$, from their mean positions, respectively. If the angular accelerations of both pendulums are same, then which expression is correct?
questions.sol:
For small swings, the angular acceleration of a simple pendulum has magnitude $\alpha=\dfrac{g}{l}\theta$.
$\dfrac{g\theta_1}{l_1}=\dfrac{g\theta_2}{l_2}$ gives $\theta_1l_2=\theta_2l_1$.

questions.text: The mean free path and the average speed of oxygen molecules at 300K and 1 atm are $3\times10^{-7}$ m and 600 m/s, respectively. Find the frequency of its collisions.
questions.sol: Collision frequency $=\dfrac{\text{average speed}}{\text{mean free path}}=\dfrac{600}{3\times10^{-7}}=2\times10^9$ s$^{-1}$.

questions.text: Two infinite identical charged sheets and a charged spherical body of charge density '$\rho$' are arranged as shown in figure. Then the correct relation between the electrical fields at A, B, C and D points is:
questions.sol:
Each sheet gives a uniform field $\dfrac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}$; between two identical positive sheets these cancel, and outside they add to $\dfrac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}$ pointing away from the sheets.
At A and B (between the sheets) only the sphere contributes, and A is nearer the sphere, so $E_A>E_B$.
At C the total field points left and at D it points right, and D is nearer the sphere; so $\vec E_C\ne\vec E_D$.

questions.text:
Two small spherical balls of mass 10g each with charges $-2\mu C$ and $2\mu C$, are attached to two ends of very light rigid rod of length 20 cm. The arrangement is now placed near an infinite non-conducting charge sheet with uniform charge density of $100\mu C/m^2$ such that length of rod makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with electric field generated by charge sheet. Net torque acting on the rod is:
(Take $\varepsilon_0$ : $8.85\times10^{-12}$ C$^2$/Nm$^2$)
questions.sol:
Field of the sheet: $E=\dfrac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}=\dfrac{100\times10^{-6}}{2\times8.85\times10^{-12}}\approx5.65\times10^{6}$ N/C.
Dipole moment $p=qd=2\times10^{-6}\times0.2=4\times10^{-7}$ C m.
$\tau=pE\sin30^\circ=4\times10^{-7}\times5.65\times10^6\times0.5\approx1.13$ N m, i.e. about 1.12 N m.

questions.text:
A small mirror of mass m is suspended by a massless thread of length $l$. Then the small angle through which the thread will be deflected when a short pulse of laser of energy E falls normal on the mirror
(c = speed of light in vacuum and g = acceleration due to gravity)
questions.sol:
The pulse carries momentum $\dfrac Ec$; on reflection the mirror receives $\dfrac{2E}{c}$, so it starts with speed $v=\dfrac{2E}{mc}$.
It then rises through $h=l(1-\cos\theta)\approx\dfrac{l\theta^2}{2}$: $v^2=2gh=gl\theta^2$, so $v=\theta\sqrt{gl}$.
$\theta=\dfrac{2E}{mc\sqrt{gl}}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: When an object is placed 40 cm away from a spherical mirror an image of magnification $\dfrac12$ is produced. To obtain an image with magnification of $\dfrac13$, the object is to be moved :
questions.sol:
A positive magnification less than 1 means an erect, diminished image: a convex mirror. With $u=-40$ cm, $m=-\dfrac vu=\dfrac12$ gives $v=20$ cm, and $\dfrac1f=\dfrac1{20}-\dfrac1{40}$, so $f=40$ cm.
For $m=\dfrac13$: $v=-\dfrac u3$, so $\dfrac1v+\dfrac1u=-\dfrac2u=\dfrac1{40}$ and $u=-80$ cm.
The object must be moved a further 40 cm away from the mirror.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R
Assertion A: In photoelectric effect, on increasing the intensity of incident light the stopping potential increases.
Reason R: Increase in intensity of light increases the rate of photoelectrons emitted, provided the frequency of incident light is greater than threshold frequency.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.sol:
The stopping potential depends only on the frequency of the light and the work function ($eV_0=h\nu-\phi$), not on intensity: A is false.
Above the threshold frequency, a higher intensity means more photons per second and so more photoelectrons per second: R is true.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text: Considering the Bohr model of hydrogen like atoms, the ratio of the radius of $5^{\text{th}}$ orbit of the electron in $\mathrm{Li^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{He^+}$ is
questions.sol:
In the Bohr model $r_n\propto\dfrac{n^2}{Z}$.
For the same $n$: $\dfrac{r_{Li^{2+}}}{r_{He^+}}=\dfrac{Z_{He}}{Z_{Li}}=\dfrac23$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
The Boolean expression $Y=A\bar BC+\bar A\bar C$ can be realised with which of the following gate configurations.
A. One 3-input AND gate, 3 NOT gates and one 2-input OR gate, One 2-input AND gate,
B. One 3-input AND gate, 1 NOT gate, One 2-input NOR gate and one 2-input OR gate
C. 3-input OR gate, 3 NOT gates and one 2-input AND gate
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A: NOT gates make $\bar A$, $\bar B$, $\bar C$; the 3-input AND gives $A\bar BC$, the 2-input AND gives $\bar A\bar C$ and the OR combines them: works.
B: one NOT makes $\bar B$ for the 3-input AND; the NOR gives $\overline{A+C}=\bar A\bar C$; the OR combines them: works.
C: $\overline{\bar A+B+\bar C}=A\bar BC$ uses the OR and all 3 NOT gates, and $\bar A\bar C$ uses the AND, but no gate is left to add the two terms: does not work.
Answer: A, B Only.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In a Young's double slit experiment, the slits are separated by 0.2 mm. If the slits separation is increased to 0.4 mm, the percentage change of the fringe width is :
questions.sol:
Fringe width $\beta=\dfrac{\lambda D}{d}\propto\dfrac1d$.
Doubling $d$ halves $\beta$: a change of $50\%$ (a decrease).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Distance between object and its image (magnified by $-\dfrac13$) is 30 cm. The focal length of the mirror used is $\left(\dfrac x4\right)$ cm, where magnitude of value of $x$ is __________
questions.sol:
$m=-\dfrac vu=-\dfrac13$: a real, inverted, diminished image from a concave mirror, with $|v|=\dfrac{|u|}{3}$ on the same side.
$|u|-|v|=\dfrac23|u|=30$ gives $|u|=45$ cm, $|v|=15$ cm.
$\dfrac1f=\dfrac1v+\dfrac1u=-\dfrac1{15}-\dfrac1{45}=-\dfrac{4}{45}$, so $f=-\dfrac{45}{4}$ cm and $|x|=45$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A circular ring and a solid sphere having same radius roll down on an inclined plane from rest without slipping. The ratio of their velocities when reached at the bottom of the plane is $\sqrt{\dfrac x5}$ where $x=$ __________
questions.note: The exact value is $x=3.5$. NTA's final key gives "3.5 OR 4", so both 3.5 and 4 are accepted.
questions.sol:
Rolling from rest through height $h$: $v^2=\dfrac{2gh}{1+k^2/R^2}$.
Ring: $\dfrac{k^2}{R^2}=1$, $v^2=gh$. Solid sphere: $\dfrac{k^2}{R^2}=\dfrac25$, $v^2=\dfrac{10}{7}gh$.
$\dfrac{v_{ring}}{v_{sphere}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{7}{10}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{3.5}{5}}$, so $x=3.5$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.text: Four capacitors each of capacitance $16\mu F$ are connected as shown in the figure. The capacitance between points A and B is :__________ (in $\mu F$).
questions.sol:
Label the capacitors 1-4 from left to right. The top wire joins the left end of 1, the junction of 2 and 3, and the right end of 4 to B. The lower wire joins the junction of 1 and 2 and the junction of 3 and 4 to A.
So each capacitor has one plate at A and the other at B: all four are in parallel.
$C_{AB}=4\times16=64\ \mu$F.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two slabs with square cross section of different materials (1, 2) with equal sides ($l$) and thickness $d_1$ and $d_2$ such that $d_2=2d_1$ and $l>d_2$. Considering lower edges of these slabs are fixed to the floor, we apply equal shearing force on the narrow faces. The angle of deformation is $\theta_2=2\theta_1$. If the shear moduli of material 1 is $4\times10^9$ N/m$^2$, then shear moduli of material 2 is $x\times10^9$ N/m$^2$, where value of $x$ is ______.
questions.sol:
The force acts on a narrow face of area $l\,d$, so the shear stress is $\dfrac{F}{ld}$ and $\theta=\dfrac{F}{l\,d\,G}$.
$\dfrac{\theta_2}{\theta_1}=\dfrac{d_1G_1}{d_2G_2}=2$ with $d_2=2d_1$ gives $G_2=\dfrac{G_1}{4}=1\times10^9$ N/m$^2$.
$x=1$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Conductor wire ABCDE with each arm 10 cm in length is placed in magnetic field of $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$ Tesla, perpendicular to its plane. When conductor is pulled towards right with constant velocity of 10 cm/s, induced emf between points A and E is __________mV.
questions.sol:
For a wire moving with velocity $\vec v$ in a uniform field, the emf between its ends is $Bv\,L_\perp$, where $L_\perp$ is the length of the straight line AE measured at right angles to $\vec v$.
AB and DE are along $\vec v$; BC and CD are at $45^\circ$ to it, each giving $10\sin45^\circ=5\sqrt2$ cm. So $L_\perp=10\sqrt2$ cm.
$\varepsilon=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\times0.1\times0.1\sqrt2=0.01$ V $=10$ mV.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Which one of the following about an electron occupying the 1s orbital in a hydrogen atom is incorrect?
(Bohr's radius is represented by $a_0$)
options: The probability density of finding the electron is maximum at the nucleus
The electron can be found at a distance $2a_0$ from the nucleus
The total energy of the electron is maximum when it is at a distance $a_0$ from the nucleus
questions.sol:
For 1s, $\psi^2$ is greatest at the nucleus (1 is correct); the probability is non-zero at any distance, including $2a_0$ (2 is correct); the orbital is spherically symmetrical (3 is correct).
The total energy of the electron in the 1s state is fixed ($-13.6$ eV); it does not depend on where the electron is found. $a_0$ is only where the radial probability is greatest. So statement (4) is incorrect.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Which of the following molecule(s) show/s paramagnetic behavior?
A. $\mathrm{O_2}$
B. $\mathrm{N_2}$
C. $\mathrm{F_2}$
D. $\mathrm{S_2}$
E. $\mathrm{Cl_2}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
In MO theory $\mathrm{O_2}$ has two unpaired electrons in the $\pi^*$ orbitals, so it is paramagnetic; $\mathrm{S_2}$ (vapour) has the same valence configuration and is also paramagnetic.
$\mathrm{N_2}$, $\mathrm{F_2}$ and $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ have all electrons paired (diamagnetic).
Answer: A & D.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Let us consider a reversible reaction at temperature, T.
In this reaction, both $\Delta H$ and $\Delta S$ were observed to have positive values. If the equilibrium temperature is Te, then the reaction becomes spontaneous at:
questions.sol:
$\Delta G=\Delta H-T\Delta S$ with $\Delta H, \Delta S>0$; at equilibrium $\Delta G=0$, so $T_e=\dfrac{\Delta H}{\Delta S}$.
$\Delta G<0$ needs $T\Delta S>\Delta H$, i.e. $T>T_e$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
One mole of an ideal gas expands isothermally and reversibly from 10 dm$^3$ to 20 dm$^3$ at 300 K. $\Delta U$, q and work done in the process respectively are
Given: R = 8.3 J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$
ln 10 = 2.3
log 2 = 0.30
log 3 = 0.48
questions.sol:
Isothermal ideal gas: $\Delta U=0$.
$w=-nRT\ln\dfrac{V_2}{V_1}=-1\times8.3\times300\times2.3\times0.30=-1718$ J $=-1.718$ kJ (work done on the gas).
$q=-w=+1.718$ kJ.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
XY is the membrane/partition between two chambers 1 and 2 containing sugar solutions of concentration $c_1$ and $c_2$ $(c_1>c_2)$ mol L$^{-1}$. For the reverse osmosis to take place identify the correct condition.
(Here $p_1$ and $p_2$ are pressures applied on chamber 1 and 2).
A. Membrane/Partition : Cellophane, $p_1>\pi$
B. Membrane/Partition : Porous, $p_2>\pi$
C. Membrane/Partition : Parchment paper, $p_1>\pi$
D. Membrane/Partition : Cellophane, $p_2>\pi$
Choose the correct answer from the option given below:
questions.sol:
Reverse osmosis needs a semipermeable membrane (cellophane and parchment paper are; a porous partition is not) and a pressure greater than the osmotic pressure applied on the more concentrated side, here chamber 1.
So the conditions are A and C.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: On charging the lead storage battery, the oxidation state of lead changes from $x_1$ to $y_1$ at the anode and from $x_2$ to $y_2$ at the cathode. The values of $x_1$, $y_1$, $x_2$, $y_2$ are respectively :
questions.note: The key's answer names the electrodes as they are named during discharge: the anode (Pb plate) goes from +2 to 0 and the cathode ($\mathrm{PbO_2}$ plate) from +2 to +4 on charging.
questions.sol:
On charging, $\mathrm{PbSO_4}$ on both plates is converted back.
At the plate that is the anode during discharge (the Pb plate): $\mathrm{PbSO_4}+2e^-\to\mathrm{Pb}+\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$: $+2\to0$.
At the plate that is the cathode during discharge (the $\mathrm{PbO_2}$ plate): $\mathrm{PbSO_4}+2\mathrm{H_2O}\to\mathrm{PbO_2}+\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}+4\mathrm{H^+}+2e^-$: $+2\to+4$.
So $x_1, y_1, x_2, y_2=+2, 0, +2, +4$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
For $\mathrm{A_2+B_2\rightleftharpoons2AB}$
$E_a$ for forward and backward reaction are 180 and 200 kJ mol$^{-1}$ respectively
If catalyst lowers $E_a$ for both reaction by 100 kJ mol$^{-1}$.
Which of the following statement is correct?
options: Catalyst can cause non-spontaneous reactions to occur.
The enthalpy change for the reaction is +20 kJ mol$^{-1}$.
The enthalpy change for the catalysed reaction is different from that of uncatalysed reaction.
Catalyst does not alter the Gibbs energy change of a reaction.
questions.sol:
$\Delta H=E_{a,f}-E_{a,b}=180-200=-20$ kJ mol$^{-1}$, with or without the catalyst (statements 2 and 3 are wrong).
A catalyst lowers both activation energies equally; it cannot change $\Delta G$, so it cannot make a non-spontaneous reaction occur.
Statement (4) is correct.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Rate law for a reaction between A and B is given by
$r=k[A]^n[B]^m$
If concentration of A is doubled and concentration of B is halved from their initial value, the ratio of new rate of reaction to the initial rate of reaction $\left(\dfrac{r_2}{r_1}\right)$ is
questions.sol: $\dfrac{r_2}{r_1}=\dfrac{k(2[A])^n\left(\frac{[B]}{2}\right)^m}{k[A]^n[B]^m}=2^n\cdot2^{-m}=2^{(n-m)}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are the pairs of group 13 elements showing their relation in terms of atomic radius.
(B < Al), (Al < Ga), (Ga < In) and (In < Tl)
Identify the elements present in the incorrect pair and in that pair find out the element (X) that has higher ionic radius $(\mathrm{M^{3+}})$ than the other one. The atomic number of the element (X) is
questions.sol:
Atomic radii: B 85, Al 143, Ga 135, In 167, Tl 170 pm. Ga is smaller than Al (poor shielding by the 3d electrons), so (Al < Ga) is the incorrect pair.
Ionic radii: $\mathrm{Al^{3+}}$ 53.5 pm, $\mathrm{Ga^{3+}}$ 62 pm, so X is Ga.
Atomic number of Ga $=31$.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Nitrogen forms oxides with +1 to +5 oxidation states due to the formation of $p\pi-p\pi$ bond with oxygen.
Statement II: Nitrogen does not form halides with +5 oxidation state due to the absence of d-orbital in it.
In the light of given statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are False
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II are true
questions.sol:
Nitrogen is small and forms strong $p\pi-p\pi$ multiple bonds with oxygen, which lets it form the oxides $\mathrm{N_2O}$ (+1) up to $\mathrm{N_2O_5}$ (+5): Statement I is true.
Nitrogen has no d orbitals in its valence shell, so it cannot expand its octet to form $\mathrm{NX_5}$: Statement II is true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Pair of transition metal ions having the same number of unpaired electrons is
questions.sol:
Unpaired electrons (free ions): $\mathrm{Ti^{2+}}$ $d^2$: 2; $\mathrm{Co^{2+}}$ $d^7$: 3; $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ $d^5$: 5; $\mathrm{Cr^{2+}}$ $d^4$: 4; $\mathrm{V^{2+}}$ $d^3$: 3; $\mathrm{Ti^{3+}}$ $d^1$: 1; $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}$ $d^5$: 5.
$\mathrm{V^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{Co^{2+}}$ both have 3.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Number of stereoisomers possible for the complexes, $\mathrm{[CrCl_3(py)_3]}$ and $\mathrm{[CrCl_2(ox)_2]^{3-}}$ are respectively
(py = pyridine, ox = oxalate)
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{[CrCl_3(py)_3]}$ is of type $\mathrm{MA_3B_3}$: fac and mer isomers, both with a mirror plane, so 2 stereoisomers.
$\mathrm{[CrCl_2(ox)_2]^{3-}}$ is of type $\mathrm{M(AA)_2B_2}$: trans (achiral) and cis, which exists as a pair of enantiomers, so 3 stereoisomers.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Which one of the following complexes will have $\Delta_o=0$ and $\mu=5.96$ B.M?
questions.sol:
$\mu=5.96$ B.M. corresponds to 5 unpaired electrons ($\sqrt{35}\approx5.92$), i.e. high-spin $d^5$: $t_{2g}^3e_g^2$, for which the crystal field stabilisation energy is zero (the "$\Delta_o=0$" of the question).
$\mathrm{[Mn(SCN)_6]^{4-}}$ has $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}$ ($d^5$) with a weak-field ligand: high spin.
The others: $\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{4-}}$ $d^6$ low spin (0 unpaired), $\mathrm{[FeF_6]^{4-}}$ $d^6$ high spin (4), $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}$ $d^6$ low spin (0).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements.
Statement I: The dipole moment of $\mathrm{\overset{4}{C}H_3-\overset{3}{C}H=\overset{2}{C}H-\overset{1}{C}H=O}$ is greater than $\mathrm{\overset{4}{C}H_3-\overset{3}{C}H_2-\overset{2}{C}H_2-\overset{1}{C}H=O}$
Statement II: $\mathrm{C_1-C_2}$ bond length of $\mathrm{\underset{4}{C}H_3-\underset{3}{C}H=\underset{2}{C}H-\underset{1}{C}H=O}$ is greater than $\mathrm{C_1-C_2}$ bond length of $\mathrm{\underset{4}{C}H_3-\underset{3}{C}H_2-\underset{2}{C}H_2-\underset{1}{C}H=O}$
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
In but-2-enal the C=C is conjugated with C=O, so the resonance form $\mathrm{CH_3-\overset{+}{C}H-CH=CH-O^-}$ contributes and charge separation is greater: its dipole moment is larger than that of butanal. Statement I is true.
The same conjugation gives the $\mathrm{C_1-C_2}$ bond partial double-bond character (and both carbons are $sp^2$), so it is shorter than in butanal. Statement II is false.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text: Benzene is treated with oleum to produce compound (X) which when further heated with molten sodium hydroxide followed by acidification produces compound (Y). The compound Y is treated with zinc metal to produce compound (Z). Identify the structure of compound (Z) from the following option.
questions.sol:
Benzene + oleum gives benzenesulphonic acid (X).
Fusion with NaOH and acidification gives phenol (Y).
Heating phenol with zinc dust removes the oxygen: benzene (Z), option (4).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Predict the major product of the following reaction sequence:-
questions.sol:
(1) Free-radical bromination of methylcyclohexane substitutes at the tertiary carbon: 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane.
(2) Alcoholic KOH eliminates HBr to give the more substituted alkene, 1-methylcyclohexene.
(3) HBr with peroxide adds anti-Markovnikov: Br goes to the less substituted ring carbon, giving 1-bromo-2-methylcyclohexane, option (4).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Aldol condensation is a popular and classical method to prepare $\alpha, \beta$-unsaturated carbonyl compounds. This reaction can be both intermolecular and intramolecular. Predict which one of the following is not a product of intramolecular aldol condensation?
questions.sol:
Options (1), (2) and (4) are enones in which the new C=C lies inside a ring; each can come from a single dicarbonyl molecule cyclising (for example, (1) from 5-oxohexanal, (2) from 2-(3-oxobutyl)cyclohexanone, (4) from 2-acetylbenzaldehyde).
Option (3) has an exocyclic $\mathrm{=CH_2}$ next to the ring C=O: that unit comes from a second molecule (methanal) condensing with $\alpha$-tetralone, an intermolecular reaction.
Answer: option (3).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: An organic compound (X) with molecular formula $\mathrm{C_3H_6O}$ is not readily oxidised. On reduction it gives $\mathrm{C_3H_8O}$(Y) which reacts with HBr to give a bromide (Z) which is converted to Grignard reagent. This Grignard reagent on reaction with (X) followed by hydrolysis give 2, 3-dimethylbutan-2-ol. Compounds (X), (Y) and (Z) respectively are:
questions.sol:
Not readily oxidised, $\mathrm{C_3H_6O}$: a ketone, acetone (X).
Reduction gives propan-2-ol (Y); HBr gives 2-bromopropane (Z); its Grignard reagent $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CHMgBr}$ adds to acetone.
Hydrolysis gives $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C(OH)CH(CH_3)_2}$, 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol, as required. Option (3).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The major product (A) formed in the following reaction sequence is
questions.sol:
(i) Sn/HCl reduces nitrobenzene to aniline. (ii) $\mathrm{Ac_2O}$/pyridine gives acetanilide, whose $\mathrm{-NHCOCH_3}$ group is a milder activator.
(iii) $\mathrm{Br_2}$/AcOH brominates once, at the para position (the bulky group hinders ortho attack).
(iv) Aqueous NaOH hydrolyses the amide: 4-bromoaniline, option (4).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Identify the pair of reactants that upon reaction, with elimination of HCl will give rise to the dipeptide Gly-Ala .
questions.sol:
In Gly-Ala, the carbonyl of glycine (the N-terminal residue) is bonded to the $\mathrm{NH}$ of alanine.
So glycine must supply an acyl chloride, $\mathrm{NH_2CH_2COCl}$, and alanine a free amino group, $\mathrm{NH_2CH(CH_3)COOH}$; they combine with loss of HCl. Option (2).
(In option (3) the alanine nitrogen is protonated and cannot attack.)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Fortification of food with iron is done using $\mathrm{FeSO_4.7H_2O}$. The mass in grams of the $\mathrm{FeSO_4.7H_2O}$ required to achieve 12 ppm of iron in 150 kg of wheat is __________ (Nearest integer)
[Given: Molar mass of Fe, S and and O respectively are 56, 32 and 16 g mol$^{-1}$]
questions.sol:
Mass of iron $=12\times10^{-6}\times150\times10^3$ g $=1.8$ g.
Molar mass of $\mathrm{FeSO_4\cdot7H_2O}=56+32+64+7\times18=278$ g mol$^{-1}$.
Mass needed $=1.8\times\dfrac{278}{56}\approx8.94$ g $\approx9$ g.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The pH of a 0.01 M weak acid HX $(K_a=4\times10^{-10})$ is found to be 5. Now the acid solution is diluted with excess of water so that the pH of the solution changes to 6. The new concentration of the diluted weak acid is given as $x\times10^{-4}$M. The value of $x$ is __________ (nearest integer)
questions.sol:
For a weak acid $[\mathrm{H^+}]=\sqrt{K_aC}$.
At pH 6: $10^{-12}=4\times10^{-10}\times C$, so $C=2.5\times10^{-3}$ M $=25\times10^{-4}$ M.
$x=25$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
In Dumas' method for estimation of nitrogen 1 g of an organic compound gave 150 mL of nitrogen collected at 300 K temperature and 900 mm Hg pressure. The percentage composition of nitrogen in the compound is __________% (nearest integer)
(Aqueous tension at 300 K = 15 mm Hg)
questions.sol:
Pressure of dry nitrogen $=900-15=885$ mm Hg.
Volume at STP $=150\times\dfrac{885}{760}\times\dfrac{273}{300}\approx159$ mL.
Mass of $\mathrm{N_2}=\dfrac{28\times159}{22400}\approx0.199$ g, so % N $\approx19.9\approx20$.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text:
The total number of hydrogen bonds of a DNA-double Helix strand whose one strand has the following sequence of bases is __________
5'- G - G-C-A-A-A-T-C-G-G-C-T-A-3'
questions.sol:
G pairs with C through 3 hydrogen bonds and A pairs with T through 2.
The strand has 7 G/C bases (G, G, C, C, G, G, C) and 6 A/T bases (A, A, A, T, T, A).
Total $=7\times3+6\times2=21+12=33$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ acts as an oxidising agent in acidic medium. 'X' is the difference between the oxidation states of Mn in reactant and product. 'Y' is the number of 'd' electrons present in the brown red precipitate formed at the end of the acetate ion test with neutral ferric chloride. The value of X + Y is __________
questions.sol:
In acid, $\mathrm{MnO_4^-}$ ($+7$) is reduced to $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}$ ($+2$): X $=5$.
The brown-red precipitate in the acetate test is basic iron(III) acetate, containing $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ ($3d^5$): Y $=5$.
X + Y $=10$.
questions.subject: Chemistry
